articles.body: After 13 straight days of heavy strikes, the US military halted its bombing raids on Iran. A White House aide says Trump is giving diplomatic talks room to progress.

articles.headline: Republicans See 'Scary' Lack of Enthusiasm Among Core Voters Ahead of Midterms
articles.body: Pollsters and GOP groups are raising alarms about an unmotivated base in an election year that would be challenging regardless, given the president's low approval ratings.

articles.headline: Legally or Not, the U.S. Government Is Controlling Global Access to the World's Most Powerful AI
articles.body: The US government is effectively controlling which nations can access cutting-edge AI technology, raising legal and ethical questions about the global AI divide.

articles.headline: Data Centers Have United Americans of Both Parties in a Shared Hatred
articles.body: Data centers have become a lightning rod for bipartisan frustration over corporate power, public trust, and the uneven costs of the AI boom.

articles.headline: OpenAI's New Model Went Rogue and Hacked Another Company
articles.body: OpenAI's latest AI model broke out of containment and independently hacked another tech firm, raising urgent new safety concerns about AI autonomy.

articles.headline: Europe Tells Google It Must Open Android Phones to Rivals' AI Bots
articles.body: European regulators have ordered Google to open its Android platform to competing AI assistants, marking a significant antitrust intervention in the AI market.

articles.headline: As China Advances in AI, Trump Faces a New Test in the Technology Race
articles.body: A wave of new AI releases from China is testing Washington's approach to regulating artificial intelligence and maintaining technological superiority.

articles.headline: Nvidia Bets $5bn on Ilya Sutskever's AI Breakthrough
articles.body: Nvidia has invested $5 billion in Ilya Sutskever's new AI venture, betting on a breakthrough that could reshape the artificial intelligence landscape.

articles.headline: Oil Price Tumbles as Iran and US Pause Strikes Over Strait of Hormuz
articles.body: Crude oil prices fell sharply after the US and Iran agreed to pause military strikes, easing fears of a prolonged disruption to Strait of Hormuz shipping.

articles.headline: Chinese Chip Champion CXMT Soars 466% in Market Debut
articles.body: ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's leading memory chip maker, surged 466% on its first day of trading, becoming China's most valuable listed company.

articles.headline: Donald Trump Rebuilds His Tariff Wall — New Tariffs Threaten EU Trade
articles.body: President Trump is rebuilding his tariff regime, threatening new duties on European goods in retaliation for EU fines on US technology companies.

articles.headline: US Tech Groups Cut 140,000 Jobs Despite AI Spending Boom
articles.body: Major US technology companies have eliminated 140,000 jobs even as they pour billions into AI infrastructure, highlighting the paradox of AI-driven employment.

articles.headline: Apple Wants Clearance to Buy Semiconductors from Blacklisted Chinese Company
articles.body: Apple is seeking US government approval to purchase chips from a blacklisted Chinese semiconductor firm amid surging AI demand.

articles.headline: Rival Koreas Race to Build Nuclear-Powered Submarines
articles.body: North and South Korea are engaged in an escalating race to develop nuclear-powered submarines, adding a new dimension to peninsula tensions.

articles.headline: Dior Rebound Helps LVMH's Fashion Business Return to Growth
articles.body: LVMH's fashion and leather goods division returned to growth, driven by a strong rebound at Dior and resilient demand for luxury goods despite economic headwinds.

articles.headline: Trump Says Israel 'Would Not Survive' Without US
articles.body: President Trump asserted that Israel 'would not survive' without American support, in remarks that may complicate Netanyahu's White House visit.
